summary: Iteration 4 covers Batch C: public subscribe API, hosted subscribe form, categories CRUD, subscribe settings, plans page + POST /plan/request, category-targeted send, custom confirm dialog, workspace-switch progress overlay, and Builder autosave. Wrote /app/backend/tests/test_batch_c.py (15 tests, all pass). Frontend Playwright verified: (1) /developers renders categories-card, form-url = https://campaigns.koodh.com/subscribe/<api_key>, api-key visible, save-subscribe-settings persists after reload, connection-card shows 'Connected' after loading the public form, regen-key-btn opens confirm-dialog, delete-category opens confirm-dialog and removes the row; (2) public /subscribe/<api_key> renders branding + category checkbox and shows subscribe-thankyou on submit (also confirmed backend creates a new contact with status=subscribed + chosen category via /public/subscribe); invalid api_key shows 'Form unavailable' page; (3) /plans shows plan-card-free|pro|enterprise, current-plan indicator, request-plan-pro opens quote-popup, request-plan-free succeeds without popup, POST /api/plan/request returns paid:true for pro/enterprise and paid:false for free; (4) Builder autosave: after fixing a runtime crash (useRef was not imported), a new campaign auto-saves within a few seconds ('Auto-saved' indicator shown), URL rewrites to /campaigns/<id>, campaign appears in list without clicking Save; (5) custom confirm dialog verified for delete-category, regen-key, and Contacts 'Delete all'; (6) workspace-switcher triggers progress-overlay checklist (Loading campaigns / Loading contacts / Refreshing dashboard) centered full-screen. Backend 15/15 passing.

minor.issue: ContactInput saves as field `category_ids`, but _start_send (and public_subscribe / list_categories.contacts count) all filter/index on field `categories`. A contact created via authenticated POST /api/contacts with category_ids=[X] is NOT reachable by SendInput.category_ids=[X] and does NOT appear in the category's contact count. Only contacts created via the public subscribe endpoint are correctly targetable. Fix: normalise to a single field name in create_contact (store as `categories`) — or map category_ids→categories on write.

Real email delivery to clara.global@koodh.com not asserted (no delivery mock configured). Endpoint returns 200 in both success and email-failure branches — an SMTP outage is silently swallowed by the try/except and only logged.

ui_bugs.issue: Runtime error 'useRef is not defined' on every visit to /campaigns/new and /campaigns/:id. useRef is used at line 43 (const hydrated = useRef(false)) but was not in the imports from 'react'. This crashed the entire builder page including autosave, block palette, canvas — replaced by the Emergent runtime-error overlay. FIXED in this iteration (added useRef to the react import). After fix, autosave, block adding, and campaign persistence all verified working.
ui_bugs.priority: HIGH (was blocking Batch C acceptance until fixed)

action_items: Verify the category/category_ids field mismatch in create_contact — currently the authenticated 'Add contact' path stores category_ids while the public subscribe / send filter / category count all use `categories`. Either alias on write or migrate to one canonical field name.
(nit) Consider surfacing plan-request email delivery failures (currently swallowed) so admins know when clara.global@koodh.com wasn't reached.
(carried over from iter_3) /api/unsubscribe/{track_id} still returns success page for unknown IDs; consider signed HMAC unsubscribe tokens.
critical_code_review_comments: Builder.js was importing { useEffect, useState, useMemo } from 'react' but calling useRef(false) — this is exactly the kind of missing-import that breaks a whole page and cannot be caught by ESLint's default config alone. Recommend enabling react/jsx-uses-react + react/react-in-jsx-scope OR a stricter no-undef rule in the frontend lint config so this fails at build.
server.py:_start_send filters contacts by field 'categories' but POST /api/contacts persists 'category_ids'. Two field names for the same concept guarantees latent bugs. Pick one and add a migration.

server.py:public_subscribe uses `$set` on first_name/last_name/city even when data.first_name is empty string — an existing contact re-subscribing with a blank form will overwrite their real names with '' (defaults on PublicSubscribeInput are ''). Only overwrite when data.first_name is non-empty.

server.py:_subscribe_out fallback for public_base uses os.environ['BACKEND_URL'] which would 500 if PUBLIC_BASE_URL is unset AND BACKEND_URL happens to be missing. Use os.environ.get(...) with a safe fallback.

server.py:GET /public/form/{api_key} silently flips api_connected=True the first time any URL is fetched — including a Playwright preflight. That is convenient for the 'Connected' checkmark but means a single OPTIONS/preview request is enough to flip state. Acceptable but worth documenting.

rca of the issue: Builder crash RCA: /app/frontend/src/pages/Builder.js line 1 imported only { useEffect, useState, useMemo } from 'react', but line 43 introduced `const hydrated = useRef(false)` for the autosave hydration guard. At runtime React evaluates useRef against the module scope and gets ReferenceError → Emergent's error boundary intercepts and shows the 'Runtime error' overlay covering the entire /campaigns/new page. Fix was one line: add useRef to the react import. After fix, autosave loop initialises correctly (hydrated flag prevents the first initial-state effect from triggering a save), and the debounced autosave writes to /api/campaigns POST → replaces URL with /campaigns/<id> → subsequent edits PUT to the same id.
